A language of paint

Demonstrate depth in conventions

Use drawing to demonstrate understanding of conventions appropriate to painting

Suggested teaching time
4–5 weeks

Timing, task steps and quantities are classroom suggestions, not NZQA grade requirements.

Read the standard (PDF)

The brief

Which painting conventions best serve the idea I want to communicate?

Investigate a self-selected subject through drawing and painting. Build an understanding of particular painting conventions, then critically choose and apply them toward an intended outcome. Aim for decisions that are visually convincing and appropriate to your own idea.

Materials & preparation

Direct observations and your own imagery, drawing book, painting media and supports selected to suit your intention, plus materials for focused surface and colour tests.

Use your own drawings and photographs as starting points. Record sources and seek permission for people, places and culturally significant material. Discuss tikanga and context with your teacher where relevant.

Artist connections

Choose the connections that serve your intention. The contemporary models offer different approaches; select a relevant comparison rather than studying every artist. These works are references, not assessment exemplars.

Investigate how composition, support and layering affect an intended outcome. Discuss the specific cultural contexts of the Māori practices; critically choose methods that are appropriate to your own inquiry.

  • Kura Te Waru Rewiri

    Contemporary Māori · Aotearoa New Zealand

    A Construction of a Past brings abstract divisions into conversation with whakapapa, memory and connections. Look closely at the relationships between rectangular forms, painted intervals and the composition as a whole.

    Christchurch Art Gallery · A Construction of a Past, 2002 · Painting investigation

  • Nikau Hindin

    Contemporary Māori · Aotearoa New Zealand

    Hindin’s aute practice connects painting, barkcloth-making and Māori knowledge. Investigate how the support, pigments and making process contribute to meaning, rather than treating the painted surface as independent of its context.

    Fondation Cartier · artist profile and aute practice · Painting investigation

  • Julie Mehretu

    Contemporary · Ethiopia / United States

    Mehretu’s layered abstractions bring drawing and painting into dialogue with place, history and movement. Follow how overlapping marks and structures can make several spatial readings coexist.

    Whitney Museum · survey, paintings and resources · Painting investigation

  • Paul Cézanne

    France

    Study the tilted table, overlapping forms and repeated touches of colour in The Basket of Apples. Investigate how a stable object can sit inside an unsettled picture space.

    Artist resource

Studio sequence

Use this as a flexible route through the learning. Let the work suggest the next move.

  1. Name the pictorial problem

    Define an intended outcome and a question about how the painting will work: for example, how compressed space might communicate unease. Gather your own subject material and identify relevant artist practices.

  2. Investigate specific conventions

    Select a small group of conventions such as figure-ground ambiguity, tonal intervals or the interaction of transparent and opaque layers. Test each with attention to the characteristics and constraints of the media.

  3. Compare meaningful alternatives

    Make related studies using different combinations. Ask what each combination does to the intended outcome. Identify what should be kept, changed or discarded.

  4. Apply with intention

    Develop more sustained drawings or paintings in which selected conventions operate together. Refine awkward or unresolved passages while preserving the intended pictorial effect.

  5. Demonstrate your understanding

    Present a focused set of work that makes your choices visible. Explain the relationship between intended outcome, chosen conventions and handling, using the actual work as evidence.

A useful studio conversation

Put two related works side by side. Describe what changed, show the evidence and explain what you will investigate next. Invite feedback, then make your own decision.

Presentation & submission

Your teacher will confirm the assessment window, support available, final evidence and local authenticity procedures. This sheet is an original teaching resource; it is not an NZQA-issued assessment. Compare NZQA’s annotated exemplars.

What changes between grades?

Student-friendly guidance adapted from the standard. The whole body of relevant evidence determines the grade; the examples below illustrate possibilities.

Grade distinctions for AS91446
GradeWhat the evidence needs to show
AchievementSelect and use painting conventions with knowledge of their characteristics.In this task: The practical work shows an understanding of the selected processes and their effects.
MeritPurposefully apply particular conventions to achieve a chosen outcome.In this task: The selected methods consistently serve the intended pictorial result.
ExcellenceCritically select and fluently apply specific conventions with depth of understanding.In this task: The combination of methods and their skilful application resolves the intended visual problem convincingly.

Authority: NZQA AS91446 achievement criteria and explanatory notes (PDF).

Watch for

Polish alone does not demonstrate critical selection of specific conventions.

Pause & reflect

What does your chosen convention allow that an alternative would not? Point to a comparison in your studies.

Teacher notes

Planning, assessment & differentiation

Look for depth of understanding demonstrated through practical selection and use. A long survey of many artists is not a substitute. Moderate against 91446 exemplars; distinguish the informed application here from the systematic idea clarification required in 3.3.

Support and stretch

For teaching practice, reduce the number of simultaneous choices, model one material process and invite oral discussion alongside drawing. Offer vocabulary prompts and accessible media. To extend the learning, ask students to compare alternatives, justify a rejection or investigate a consequence of their own decision. Adapt assessed support to the standard’s conditions and any approved arrangements.

Before issuing the task

Set local start and finish dates, agree available materials and check the current standard, conditions and exemplars. Use school authenticity processes and your normal moderation procedures. Adjust this brief to the class and context; it has not been quality assured by NZQA.
